title: Cube-and-Conquer SAT Solving Settles & Formally Verifies Erdős’s 46-Year-Old Empty Hexagon Number h(6) = 30
aiSystem: Cube-and-Conquer SAT Solver (CaDiCaL + Lean 4 / Isabelle Verification — CMU / TU Berlin)
whyItMatters: Resolved Paul Erdős’s 1978 Empty Hexagon problem after 46 years—proving that every 30 planar points in general position contain an empty convex hexagon (h(6) = 30)—with end-to-end machine verification in Lean 4 and Isabelle.
summary: Posted in March 2024 (arXiv:2403.00737) and formally verified in ITP 2024 (arXiv:2403.17370, doi:10.4230/LIPIcs.ITP.2024.35) by Marijn J. H. Heule (Carnegie Mellon University) and Manfred Scheucher (TU Berlin), with Lean 4 formalization by Bernardo Subercaseaux, Wojciech Nawrocki, James Gallicchio, and Cayden Codel, this milestone settled Paul Erdős’s 1978 Empty Hexagon conjecture—the discrete-geometry cousin of the Happy Ending Problem. While Overmars (2003) constructed 29 points with no empty convex hexagon (h(6) ≥ 30) and Nicolás/Gerken proved h(6) existed (bounded above by 463), the exact value remained open for 46 years. Encoding planar point-set orientations via symmetry-broken propositional clauses and solving via Cube-and-Conquer SAT (~17,300 CPU hours), the authors proved h(6) = 30 and certified both the SAT unsatisfiability proof and the geometric encoding completely inside Lean 4 and Isabelle.
technicalHighlights: Proved the exact 1978 Erdős Empty Hexagon Number h(6) = 30, closing the 46-year gap between Overmars’s 29-point lower bound and prior upper bounds.
Combined geometric symmetry breaking with parallel Cube-and-Conquer SAT solving (~17,300 CPU hours) producing checkable LRAT unsatisfiability certificates.
End-to-end verified in Lean 4 (ITP 2024) confirming both the propositional proof and the geometric soundness of the SAT encoding.
caveats: Proof relies on exhaustive machine-verified case analysis via SAT certificates rather than a short human-readable synthetic geometric proof.

scoreRationale.foundational: Exact resolution of a famous 46-year-old Erdős discrete-geometry problem closely tied to the Erdős–Szekeres Happy Ending theorem.
scoreRationale.ripple: Set the gold standard for end-to-end formally verified SAT encodings bridging geometric axiomatics and industrial-scale SAT certificates in Lean 4.
scoreRationale.verification: End-to-end formally verified in Lean 4 (ITP 2024) and independently checked via certified LRAT proof checkers.
scoreRationale.velocity: Resolved a 46-year-old open discrete-geometry problem in ~17,300 CPU hours after clever symmetry breaking.
